counterexample.initialized_ticks: 50 (liquidityNet +L1), 100 (liquidityNet +L2) and 200 (liquidityNet -(L1+L2)), from positions over [50, 200) with L1 and [100, 200) with L2
counterexample.note: Tick 50 is set in the same bitmap word below tick 100, so the patch sets its advance flag back to true and skips the start tick. Active liquidity is L1 + L2 at 100 and 0 at 0, but the walk ends at L2.

summary: When the start tick is aligned and initialized, the patch skips the advance only if the start sits at bit 0 or no lower initialized tick is in the same bitmap word. Otherwise it still calls _advanceToNextDown, which skips the start tick.
